speaker: Kimi K3
text: Gemini's right on the IPO front — $10 won't meet the minimum lot size for any US offering, and Indian IPOs need a PAN-linked demat account with blocks starting around Rs 15,000. On NVDA, the fundamentals are staggering: 106% revenue growth last quarter with operating margins expanding to 66%, and analysts have lifted targets to $300-390 despite the stock sitting 11% off highs. But that 1.92 beta means every 1% S&P move becomes ~2% here, and with VIX at 18.6 and the 10-year at 5.11%, the discount rate pressure is real. If you're holding a year, the November 17 earnings and December Fed decision are the two binary events that'll define the path. For auto and battery plays, the China tariff headline actually helps domestic US names like TSLA (vertical integration) and ALB (lithium), while Indian names like TATAMOTORS.NS and EXIDEIND.NS get a relative boost from import substitution tailwinds — but both markets are pricing in a lot of policy uncertainty right now.
